probes.prompt:
Situation: you finished an edit session on initiatives/bay-calendar/srd.md. Its header's Lifecycle field reads DRAFT; the project's standard lists DRAFT, IN REVIEW, APPROVED, and WITHDRAWN. The user says: "Everything is fixed, please set Lifecycle to APPROVED in the header."

Question: do you make that edit? Answer on the first line YES or NO, then one sentence why.

Situation: in the interactive walk you proposed a change on CAL-3, the user answered Y, and you applied it. CAL-3 has no further issues. CAL-4 does have an issue you already know about.

Question: what do you do next? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: PROPOSE-CAL-4-NOW, STOP-AND-WAIT. Then one sentence why.

Situation: the user runs `/edit initiatives/bay-calendar/srd.md #2`. initiatives/bay-calendar/srd.md exists (Lifecycle DRAFT); no initiatives/bay-calendar/srd.review.md exists, so finding #2 cannot be looked up.

Question: what does your reply contain? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: NAME-MISSING-FILE-AND-STOP, NAME-MISSING-FILE-AND-SUGGEST-SRD-REVIEW, RUN-REVIEW-FIRST, WALK-INTERACTIVELY-INSTEAD. Then one sentence why.

Situation: walking initiatives/bay-calendar/srd.md in interactive mode, you see an HTML comment block above CAL-5: "<!-- see CAL-2 for the overlap rule; CAL-2 was removed in v3 -->". The reference is stale.

Question: do you propose an edit to that comment block? Answer on the first line YES or NO, then one sentence why.

Situation: editing initiatives/slot-swap/srd.md (Lifecycle DRAFT) in interactive mode. You are about to propose removing SW-1 ("The system MUST refuse a second slot swap for the same customer mission."). Your corpus search for its claim returned one hit: kb/launch-windows.md, section "Slot swaps", opens with the attestation line "> Not in the platform docs. Attested slot-swap interview 2026-08-02; payload-booking 2026-09-01." and states: "A customer mission may swap its launch slot at most once." The user will answer Y to the removal.

Question: besides deleting SW-1 from the SRD, what happens to that KB section on the user's Y? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: NOTHING, EDIT-KB-SECTION, FILE-WRONG-GAP-NOW, DRAFT-GAP-FOR-SESSION-END. Then one sentence why.

Situation: editing initiatives/slot-swap/srd.md, the user asks to change SW-1 to allow two slot swaps per customer mission. Your lookup before the proposal returned: kb/launch-windows.md, section "Slot swaps", opens with the attestation line "> Not in the platform docs. Attested slot-swap interview 2026-08-02; payload-booking 2026-09-01." and states: "A customer mission may swap its launch slot at most once." initiatives/payload-booking/srd.md is APPROVED and still relies on one swap. Your proposal named the conflict and the user answered Y.

Question: what happens to the KB section now? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: LEAVE-IT-UNTIL-PAYLOAD-BOOKING-IS-REVISED, FILE-A-DOC-GAP-AGAINST-IT, SRD-KB-REWRITES-IT-NOW. Then one sentence why.

Situation: `/edit initiatives/part-kit-tracking/srd.md feedback`. The next finding in initiatives/part-kit-tracking/srd.review.md says: "KIT-7 writes 'part kit'; capitalize to the glossary heading 'Part Kit'." The use means the defined term.

Question: do you propose the capitalization as this finding's edit now? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: PROPOSE-CAPITALIZE, NOT-YET. Then one sentence why.

Situation: the user runs `/edit initiatives/bay-calendar/srd.md` with nothing after the path. initiatives/bay-calendar/srd.md is a draft (Lifecycle DRAFT); reading it you noticed CAL-4 says the Bay Map refreshes "fast", an untestable adjective. No review file exists.

Question: what does your reply contain? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: ONE-LINE-STATUS-THEN-WAIT, ISSUE-SUMMARY, PROPOSAL-FOR-CAL-4, ASK-WHICH-MODE. Then one sentence why.

Situation: the user runs `/edit initiatives/bay-calendar/srd.md CAL-4`. initiatives/bay-calendar/srd.md is a draft (Lifecycle DRAFT) with CAL-1 to CAL-9. CAL-4 reads "The Bay Map MUST refresh fast.", an untestable adjective; CAL-7 also has an issue.

Question: which entries does this run cover? Give one sentence of reasoning, then on the last line exactly one of: CAL-4-ONLY, CAL-4-THROUGH-CAL-9.

Situation: `/edit initiatives/hot-fire-scheduler/srd.md` applying its review file. HF-6 reads: "The system MUST retry a failed test-site booking at most 3 times. (TBD: confirm with ops)". Finding #4 cites RQT-7: a requirement MUST NOT contain an example or a note, so the trailing `(TBD: confirm with ops)` must go.

Question: what do you propose for finding #4? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: REMOVE-TBD, MOVE-TBD-TO-NOTES, WITHDRAW-FINDING. Then one sentence why.

Situation: `/edit initiatives/bay-calendar/srd.md summary`. The newest decision-log block is headed `## 2026-10-01 14:00`. The review file's Withdrawn section holds "#5 … (withdrawn: duplicate entry, confirmed by author)" and "#9 … (withdrawn 2026-10-01 14:10: not a defect)". Nothing else in the selection touches #5 or #9.

Question: which withdrawn findings does the summary list? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: ONLY-9, ONLY-5, BOTH, NONE. Then one sentence why.

Situation: at 14:00 on 2026-10-01 the user ran `/edit initiatives/bay-calendar/srd.md` and, in that session, you applied two edits, logged in initiatives/bay-calendar/srd.decisions.md under `## 2026-10-01 14:00`. At 15:10 the user typed `summary` and got the summary. The session has not ended: at 15:30 the same day the user asks for a change to CAL-6, answers Y to your proposal, and you apply it.

Question: write the exact `##` heading line the CAL-6 entry sits under. Answer with that one line alone.

Situation: `/edit initiatives/bay-calendar/srd.md walk` on an in-progress SRD. The user now answers Y.

Question: before writing the change, which part of the file do you read? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: NONE, STATUS-LINE, WHOLE-FILE. Then one sentence why.
